Hi Laura / Alice —

Attached is the current subprocessor roster (redwood_subprocessor_roster_20260202.csv) and a short SIG excerpt that covers our data transfer and encryption responsibilities (redwood_sig-evidence_excerpt.pdf). Quick notes:

- Keys & residency: Customer-managed keys (CloudKMS/HSM) are supported. For EU-hosted private deployments we can enforce keys in GCP-EU or Azure-EU regions; for hosted customers we default to provider-managed envelope keys but do not export customer keys outside the chosen region.
- KV/prefix cache: ephemeral in-region caches are used to reduce latency; cached material does not contain raw customer PII and is encrypted at rest with keys scoped to the region.
- Third-party runtime deps: most inference runtime libs are open-source; Marissa will provide the SBOM excerpt for the inference side.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20260202.csv, redwood_sig-evidence_excerpt.pdf

Let me know if you want the roster broken out by environment (prod/stage) or by vendor category.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber

Subject: Follow-up: a couple clarifications on KV caching and SOC 2 scope

Laura —

Thanks for the roster and SIG excerpt. A couple quick clarifications from CardioCloud security:

1) SOC 2: can you confirm the coverage window for your most recent SOC 2 Type II (reporting period)? We need the month range and whether inference runtime (GPU pools) was in scope.
2) KV cache residency: you mentioned ephemeral in-region caches — can you confirm whether any cache replication crosses regions for failover, and if so whether replication is encrypted end-to-end and limited to supplier-owned endpoints?

Also, please provide a CAIQ mapping (matrix) showing which CAIQ control IDs are covered by Redwood policies/docs and where evidence lives (Drive link or doc references). That will speed our review.

If possible we'd like a short con-call to resolve the KV replication question; can you propose a couple time windows?

Best,
CardioCloud Security
From: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
To: sec@cardiocloud.health, alice.martin@cardiocloud.health
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 27 Jan 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: a couple clarifications on KV caching and SOC 2 scope

Hi Alice / CardioCloud team —

Thanks — quick answers below and links to a short mapping pack we've assembled.

1) SOC 2 Type II: reporting period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31. Inference runtime (dedicated and hosted GPU pools) was included in scope for control domains relevant to system availability, change management, and encryption. We can provide the SOC 2 cover letter and control map under NDA / secure link.

2) KV cache replication: we do not perform cross-region replication of ephemeral KV caches for hosted customers by default. For Dedicated/Private deployments customers may opt into cross-region failover; in those cases replication is configured over TLS, encrypted with the region-scoped keys, and limited to our provider-managed endpoints. We log replication events and provide telemetry for audits.

3) CAIQ mapping: short mapping table -> Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qAEXAMPLE_REDWOOD_SIG_EVIDENCE (contains a CAIQ-to-doc map and the SIG excerpt).

We've also uploaded: redwood_sig-evidence_excerpt.pdf (controls + evidence refs) and redwood_subprocessor_roster_20260202.csv.

If you'd like a 20–30 min call I can propose slots:
- Thu Feb 4 09:00-09:30 CET
- Thu Feb 4 14:00-14:30 CET
- Fri Feb 5 08:00-08:30 CET

Also attached is a DocuSign link (DOCUSIGN-98765) for our standard subprocessor addendum if you want to proceed with a contractual flow — you can redline and return.

Thanks,
